Lack Of Brakes Produces Bad Breaks
54
B4
Harry Goode Photos
Early in last summer's 200 mile big car race, Art Pollard of Medford, Ore. (#16-Thermo-King T. C. Offy)
lost his brakes going into the north turn. Hot on his exhaust stacks was Al Unser of Albuquerque, N. M. (#5-
Retzloff Chemical Ford). Pollard spun and hit the wall and Unser did likewise (see upper photo) as Wally
Dallenbach of New Brunswick, N. J., tosses a quick look as he speeds past. In the lower photo, Unser heads
for the fence as emergency crewmen of Wisconsin Auto Racing hotfoot it to the scene. Neither driver was
injured.

USAC Speed Stars Loaf On Pace Lap
Russ Lake Photc
Gordon Johncock of Hastings, Mich. (#3-Gilmore Broadcasting Ford) and Joe Leonard of San Jose, Calif.
(#4-Foyt Coyote) paced the starting field for the June 150 miler here last year as 24 of the nation's speedsters
got ready for the race. Johncock came on to win the race, averaging more than 98 miles per hour. Pre-race
favorite Mario Andretti of Nazareth, Pa., had been knocked out of contention when his car was wrecked in a
practice session mishap started by another driver.

Hasty Leadfoot From Hastings
Harry Goode Photo
Gordon Johncock of Hastings, Mich. (#3-Gilmore Broadcasting Ford) was on the move and heading for
victory in the June 4, 150 miler here last year when this picture was taken. Gordon is a product of the rough,
tough supermodified stock car circuit in the Detroit area which also produced John Conely, Ronnie Duman,
and Gordy's cousin, Nolan Johncock. Johncock came back to finish fourth in the Aug. 20, 200 miler and won
the "outstanding driver for 1968 at Milwaukee" award given by the Miller Brewing Co.
